taylor (Customer): Hey team, running into a lot of 429s this morning when hitting the text-generation endpoint with our 64k+ context windows. It works normally at smaller contexts. Happens intermittently but spikes during batch uploads. Example response headers pasted below, can you help? :frowning:

sam (Support): Sorry you're blocked — can you paste the full response headers + which model variant you're calling? Also are you on Hosted or Dedicated?

taylor (Customer): Hosted. Model is rwd-large-64k (we switched from rwd-large-32k last week). Here's a curl repro and headers we saw:  

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_***' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\n  -d '{"model":"rwd-large-64k","prompt":"<huge payload...>","max_tokens":512}'
```

Response (truncated):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1678901234
X-Model-RPM: 60
X-Model-TPM: 3000
Retry-After: 30
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","message":"per-model TPM exceeded"}
```

sam (Support): Thanks — that looks like TPM exhaustion on the model level. A few quick checks: are these single huge requests (high tokens per request) or many small requests? Also roughly how many requests/minute are you sending when this spikes?

taylor (Customer): It's a mix: we have a background importer that sends ~30 req/min with an average of 6k tokens/request during the spike. Outside spikes we send ~10 req/min.

elena (SRE): Jumping in — important distinction: our per-model RPM/TPM quotas measure token throughput (TPM) and request rate (RPM) separately. The 64k context increases tokens consumed per request massively, so even 30 r/m * 6k tokens = 180k tokens/min, which can blow past a model TPM that is tuned for smaller contexts. Also there's a concurrent request cap per model instance which manifests as queueing and 429s when the runtime rejects excess concurrency.

mike (Runtime Eng): To add: TPM is calculated from tokens in + tokens out over a sliding 60s window. For hosted customers we enforce both: a soft RPM and TPM and a hard max concurrency per model shard. The headers Taylor pasted show X-Model-TPM=3000 (looks like a model-level configured baseline for that tenant) and Remaining=0. That matches hitting the TPM. In short: large context -> token surge -> TPM exhausted -> 429 with Retry-After.

sam (Support): Recommended immediate mitigations: 1) throttle importer to reduce requests/min temporarily, 2) lower max_tokens or trim prefixes on the huge requests, 3) switch to a shorter context model variant for bulk-ingest (e.g., rwd-large-32k or rwd-medium-64k) or 4) request a temporary Dedicated burst for this workload. Any of those would reduce TPM pressure.

taylor (Customer): Is there a way to make the API queue requests instead of returning 429s? We thought some buffering was supported.

elena (SRE): We do limited queueing but not indefinite buffering — queue length is bounded to preserve latency SLOs for other customers. When backpressure is high we prefer deterministic 429s + Retry-After so callers can implement exponential backoff. If you need buffering semantics you should use a worker queue on your side or apply our client-side rate limiter.

mike (Runtime Eng): Also note concurrency limits are per model variant + per-tenant. If your workload has a few concurrent long-context requests those occupy GPU slots longer. Example: two 60s requests tie up concurrency 2x longer than short requests, so effective throughput drops. For throughput-heavy ingestion, prefer smaller batches or stream_chunks so each RPC is shorter-lived.

sam (Support): For us to escalate to Capacity Ops / get a short-term uplift we need: a sample of the importer request pattern (timestamps + tokens per request), the API key used (we'll redact), and desired target throughput (e.g., want to sustain X tokens/min). Can you paste that?

taylor (Customer): Pasting sample log snippet:  

```
2026-02-28T09:12:01Z importer#1 req_id=abc tokens_in=5200 tokens_out=420 duration_ms=34000
2026-02-28T09:12:03Z importer#1 req_id=abd tokens_in=6100 tokens_out=510 duration_ms=36000
2026-02-28T09:12:05Z importer#2 req_id=abe tokens_in=4800 tokens_out=400 duration_ms=32000
```

sam (Support): Perfect. Filing to Capacity with these logs. In the meantime you can implement a leaky-bucket limiter: target ~10 req/min or reduce tokens per req to stay under the 3000 TPM shown. Quick calc: target_TPM / avg_tokens_per_request = safe_rpm. Example: 3000 TPM / 6000 tokens = 0.5 req/min -> you'll need dedicated capacity if you need higher concurrency with those token sizes.

elena (SRE): Another option is model-variant fallback policy: route large-context imports to a Dedicated pool or a cheaper quantized variant that has higher TPM caps. Also check your account-level global quotas — sometimes account-level billing issues can cause temporary hard caps; @sam can check billing state for Taylor.

ci-bot: Capacity request created: CAP-9876 assigned to ops-team. ETA 4h for initial review.

sam (Support): I checked billing — no blocks. I've attached CAP-9876 and assigned to runtime for review. Will update here after ops triage. For now please implement the temporary throttle and retry logic, and consider batching fewer docs per request. :thumbsup:

taylor (Customer): Thanks everyone — we'll pause the importer and implement a backoff. Appreciate the quick help.

mike (Runtime Eng): Quick tech note to keep: when you measure token usage, count prompt + response tokens. And be cautious: context-length increases both memory (may force a different kernel) and TPM cost. If you want, we can run a short eval with your workload on a Dedicated trial to estimate needed commit.

sam (Support): Adding follow-ups for docs team: create an ops KB for customers about "large-context ingestion best practices" covering TPM math, concurrency effects, and fallback patterns. Filing internal doc ticket DOC-412.

taylor (Customer): Cool — will await CAP-9876 updates. Thanks! :pray:
